Part 1

What does each drawing show, and what are the blocks of a crude unit?

Part 1 · the plan

Three drawings, seven blocks

  1. BFD, PFD, P&IDeach drawing answers a different question at a different stage
  2. The BFD of this unitseven process steps and 23 flags
  3. Why each block is thereequipment inside, flags in and out, heat it trades

Step 1 · three drawings

Each drawing answers a different question

BFDPFDP&ID
A box isa process stepone item of equipment, with its tagevery line, valve, instrument, trip
Streams carrya flag and a stream tablea flag and the full balanceline numbers; no flows

Start where design starts: the BFD.

Step 2 · interactive · the BFD of V-1

Follow one colour at a time

Each colour is one kind of stream; blue crude enters once and leaves split into five products.

Step 3 · interactive · click a block

Seven blocks, seven reasons

A block is a process step, not a piece of equipment: four exchangers that do one job share one block.

Part 1 · summary

What Part 1 settled

  • BFD = steps, PFD = equipment and balance, P&ID = everything to build and protect.
  • The crude unit has seven blocks: cold preheat to overhead system.
  • Heat trades between blocks without mixing streams.

Blocks are joined by flags. Next: what each flag carries, and whether it all balances.

Part 2

What do the streams carry, and does the unit balance?

Part 2 · the plan

Flags, boundaries and accumulation

  1. The stream table23 flags, each with flow, temperature and pressure
  2. Boundary balancein − out = accumulation, around any block
  3. The unit in motionwhat the balance shows while the simulator moves
  4. Energy balancesheater H-1 and column V-1 close at design

Step 1 · interactive · click a flag

Every flag is one row of the stream table

Flows are liquid m³/h unless the flag says otherwise; the drawing stays readable because the numbers live in the table.

Interactive · simulator runs

A step upsets the balance until the levels settlestep 2 of 2

whole unit$\sum \dot m_{in} - \sum \dot m_{out} = dM/dt$

A non-zero sum is inventory moving: the levels absorb it, then the level loops hand it downstream and the sum returns to zero.

Part 2 · summary

What Part 2 settled

  • 23 flags, one stream-table row each, design and live.
  • In − out = accumulation: zero at steady state, not during a change.
  • Heater and column close on energy; pumparounds carry heat to preheat.

The BFD hides the equipment. Next: the PFD, where every item has a tag.

3

Part 3

How do you read the PFD and check its flags against the model?

Part 3 · the plan

One sheet, read in four moves

  1. The main process linecrude from storage to the flash zone
  2. The equipment listtag, service and design duty of each item
  3. Flags against the modelTurton flag shapes and 19 checked values
  4. What the P&ID addswhat the PFD deliberately leaves out

Step 1 · interactive · PFD-ACU-01 rev 0

Follow the heavy line from storage to V-1

Feed left, products right, numbers 1–23 are the same flags as the BFD; 24 and up are links inside one block.

Step 2 · interactive · click a tag

Every item has a tag, a service and a duty

The preheat train recovers 29.4 MW from eleven exchangers, more than the 22.3 MW the heater adds.

Step 3 · interactive · Turton flags

Three shapes, three quantities, one check

Parallelogram = mass flow (t/h), rectangle = temperature (°C), trapezoid = pressure (kPa g); all 19 flag values agree with the model.

Step 4 · beyond the PFD

What the P&ID adds

ItemOn the PFDOn the P&ID
Pumpsone symbol per serviceA and B, strainers, check valves, minimum flow
Controlvalves that define the processevery loop, cascade, split range
Safetynonerelief valves, heater EMS, alarms
Heaterone symboltwo pass loops, fuel trains, pilot, atomising steam
Datadesign flow, T, P on flagsranges and set points; no flows

Part 3 · summary

What Part 3 settled

  • Read the PFD along the heavy line, then the side loops.
  • Each tag carries a service and a design duty you can check live.
  • Flag shapes code the quantity; values come from the model.
  • Loops, trips and line data belong to the P&ID.

To keep

Key Takeaways

1

Choose the drawing by the question: steps, equipment, or everything to build.

2

Give every flag one stream-table row; keep numbers off the drawing.

3

Read a non-zero balance as inventory moving, not as a lost stream.

4

Check every flag value against the model before you issue a PFD.
